summary.title: Code as Agent Harness: Toward Executable, Verifiable, and Stateful Agent Systems

details: Existing surveys treat code mainly as the end product of LLMs, leaving underexplored the role of 'agent-initiated code artifacts' (tests, temporary tools, DSL programs, executable workflows, reusable skills, program state) that agents create, execute, revise, persist, and share inside the task loop.

The bottleneck of agent autonomy is argued to lie not only in model reasoning but in the surrounding harness (tools, sandboxes, memory, validators, permission tiers, execution loops, feedback channels) that turns a stateless model into a long-running agent.

Conceptual framing of 'code as agent harness': code as the executable, inspectable, and stateful medium through which agents reason, act, model environments, verify progress, persist state, and coordinate.

A three-layer taxonomy organizing the literature: (1) harness interface (code for reasoning, acting, environment modeling); (2) harness mechanisms (planning, memory/context engineering, tool use, Plan-Execute-Verify control, agentic harness engineering); (3) scaling the harness to multi-agent orchestration over shared code artifacts.

Explicit distinction among model-internal capabilities, system-provided harness infrastructure, and agent-initiated code artifacts, with a scope boundary defining 'code' as executable or machine-checkable artifacts (programs, specs, proof scripts, tool schemas, tests, repositories, simulators, traces/logs).
Literature up to 2026, with per-layer roadmaps and comparison tables of representative systems annotated by mechanism, paradigm, and key innovation.

Layer 1 subdivided into: program-delegated reasoning (PAL, PoT, CodeI/O), formal/symbolic interfaces (SATLM, Lean-based provers, Lean4Agent), iterative code-grounded reasoning (NExT, CodePRM, RLEF, EG-CFG); code-for-acting into grounded skill selection (SayCan, KnowNo), programmatic policy generation (Code-as-Policies, Code-BT), lifelong code agents (Voyager, UI-Voyager); code-for-environment into structured world representations, execution-trace world models (WorldCoder, CWM), code-grounded evaluation (SWE-bench, InterCode, CRUXEval), and verifiable environment construction (SWE-smith, EnvScaler).

Planning grouped by locus of harness control: linear decomposition (Self-Planning, WebAgent, PLAN.md-style persistent artifacts), structure-grounded (CodePlan, repo/knowledge graphs, AGENTS.md), search-based (CodeTree, MCTS/SWE-Search, Meta-Harness), orchestration-based (MapCoder, natural-language agent harnesses).
Memory grouped by functional role: working, semantic, experiential, long-term, multi-agent memory, plus cross-cutting context compaction and state offloading (LongCodeZip, SWE-Pruner).

Tool use grouped by harness function: function-oriented (ToolCoder, RAG-for-code), environment-interaction (SWE-agent, CodeAgent), verification-driven (AgentCoder, VeriGuard), workflow-orchestration (ToolNet, OpenHands), with tool lifecycle hooks and permission gating.

Plan-Execute-Verify (PEV) loop reframing feedback-guided debugging: plans as contracts over intended state transitions; sandboxed, multi-tier permissioned execution (read-only, sandbox-edit, full-access with human-in-the-loop gates); verification via deterministic sensors (linters, type checkers, tests, fuzzers, CI).

Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE): deep telemetry (prompts, cost, latency, tool arguments, diffs, traces, rejected branches, human interventions) as optimization substrate; an 'Evolution Agent' loop of observe-diagnose-propose-evaluate-promote; governed harness mutation subject to sandboxed evaluation, regression suites, and HITL approval for permission-boundary changes.

Multi-agent section catalogs role specialization (planner, synthesizer, verifier, executor, reviewer), interaction modes (collaborative synthesis, critique-repair, debate, delegation, search), and topologies (chain/waterfall, hierarchical, cyclic, adaptive) across ChatDev, MetaGPT, MAGIS, HyperAgent, Trae Agent, FlowReasoner, and others, with harness substrate labeled per system (blackboard, repository, execution).
Application domains: coding assistance/issue resolution, GUI and OS automation, embodied control and personalization, scientific discovery, DevOps and enterprise workflows.

key_findings.finding: Code is best understood as the operational harness of agentic systems rather than as a generated artifact, defined by three functional properties: executability, inspectability, and statefulness.
key_findings.evidence: The survey argues these are not merely notational properties but harness functions: executability lets the harness verify intended actions, inspectability lets failures be diagnosed and fed back, and statefulness preserves interaction history across steps; it further sets a scope boundary excluding raw perception, physical state, human intent, and latent model reasoning from 'code'.

key_findings.finding: A three-way decomposition of long-running agent systems isolates agent-initiated code artifacts as the underexplored component.
key_findings.evidence: Model-internal capabilities, system-provided harness infrastructure (tools, sandboxes, validators, permission tiers, telemetry), and agent-initiated code artifacts (regression tests, temporary tools, DSL programs, executable workflows, reusable skills, intermediate program state) are distinguished, with the latter identified as the survey's focus and illustrated via Claude Code, Codex, and LangChain-style harnesses.

key_findings.finding: Iterative debugging, planning, and verification are unified as a single harness-level control loop (Plan-Execute-Verify) governed by deterministic sensors and permission tiers.
key_findings.evidence: The survey recasts plans as explicit contracts specifying editable files, invariants, validation commands, and rollback points; execution as bounded transitions in sandboxes with read-only / sandbox-edit / full-access tiers and mandatory HITL gates for irreversible actions; and verification as compiler, static-analysis, runtime, and test sensors that also govern termination, arguing reflection is reliable only when grounded in executable evidence.

key_findings.finding: The harness itself can be treated as an object of measurement and optimization (Agentic Harness Engineering), distinct from prompt and context engineering.
key_findings.evidence: Deep telemetry linking prompts, cost, latency, tool arguments, diffs, test outcomes, rejected alternatives, and human interventions is proposed as the optimization substrate; an Evolution Agent observes, diagnoses, proposes, evaluates on held-out or replayed traces, and promotes only non-regressing revisions, with AutoHarness, Meta-Harness, GEPA, EvoMAC, and observability stacks synthesized as three complementary strands.

key_findings.finding: Reported gains from planning and memory mechanisms are confounded with harness and evaluation conditions, making harness-aware evaluation an open problem.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion notes that conclusions depend on execution environments, feedback quality, tool access, trajectory budgets, test sufficiency, log-parsing correctness, and benchmark contamination; if benchmarks fail to stress long-range dependency management or if environments drift, apparent improvements may reflect environment noise rather than agent-level capability.
